units.explain: Normalizes a config value into a timedelta. Returns the value unchanged when it is None or already a timedelta; otherwise it treats the int as a number of seconds and wraps it in timedelta(seconds=value). Pure function, no side effects, no exceptions beyond what the timedelta constructor may raise for bad ints.
units.summary: Coerce None/timedelta/int session-lifetime values to a timedelta or None.

relations.basis: passed as get_converter for the permanent_session_lifetime ConfigAttribute

uncertainties: Non-int, non-timedelta, non-None values are not handled explicitly; behavior depends on timedelta(seconds=...) semantics

units.explain: Sans-IO application core: subclass of Scaffold holding configuration attributes, extension points (class attributes like aborter_class, jinja_environment, app_ctx_globals_class, config_class, json_provider_class, url_rule_class, url_map_class), and ConfigAttribute-backed settings (testing/TESTING, secret_key/SECRET_KEY, permanent_session_lifetime/PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME with _make_timedelta converter). The class body also contains small lifecycle guards and accessors explained elsewhere; it defines no I/O itself. Overridable class attributes let subclasses swap implementations (config, JSON provider, routing rule/map classes, Jinja environment). Members folded here: _check_setup_finished (raises AssertionError if any setupmethod is invoked after the first request, keyed on _got_first_request), make_aborter (returns self.aborter_class(), default Aborter), iter_blueprints (returns self.blueprints.values() in registration order), and create_jinja_environment (abstract stub raising NotImplementedError; the concrete Flask subclass must supply it). Boundary: mutating testing/secret_key/permanent_session_lifetime writes through ConfigAttribute to self.config; permanent_session_lifetime accepts int seconds via the converter.
units.summary: Sans-IO application core: config attributes, pluggable class hooks, and setup guards.
uncertainties: Exact behavior of ConfigAttribute get/set delegation lives in flask/config.py, not shown here

units.explain: Constructor. Delegates import_name/static_folder/static_url_path/template_folder/root_path handling to Scaffold.__init__, then: derives instance_path (auto-find when not given; ValueError when a relative path is supplied), builds self.config via make_config(instance_relative_config), creates self.aborter via make_aborter, instantiates self.json from json_provider_class, and initializes empty registries: url_build_error_handlers, teardown_appcontext_funcs, shell_context_processors, blueprints (ordered dict), extensions. Creates self.url_map = url_map_class(host_matching=host_matching), stores subdomain_matching, and sets _got_first_request=False which gates all setupmethods. No returns; failure exits are the relative-instance-path ValueError and anything raised by Scaffold.__init__/make_config.
units.summary: Initialize instance path, config, aborter, JSON provider, registries, and URL map.

extras.note: Sets _got_first_request=False, enabling the setup-finished guard for all decorated setup methods.

uncertainties: Scaffold.__init__ behavior (root_path detection, static route setup) is defined in scaffold.py, outside this batch

units.explain: Cached property resolving the display name. If import_name is '__main__', it reads the __main__ module's __file__; when that attribute is missing it returns the literal '__main__', otherwise the file's basename without extension. For any other import_name it returns it verbatim. Cached via werkzeug's cached_property, so the first access fixes the value for the instance's lifetime.
units.summary: Application display name, derived from __main__'s file when import name is __main__.
uncertainties: cached_property stores into instance __dict__; later changes to import_name are ignored

units.explain: Cached property returning a logging.Logger via flask.logging.create_logger(self). The docstring records the contract: named after app.name, level set to DEBUG in debug mode, and a default handler added only when no handlers exist. All actual behavior (level, handler setup) is delegated to create_logger, an unproven boundary in flask/logging.py.
units.summary: Return the app's Logger, created lazily by create_logger.
uncertainties: Level/handler behavior depends on create_logger, not visible here

units.explain: Groups the lazy Jinja environment lifecycle. jinja_env is a cached property calling create_jinja_environment() on first access; in this sans-io class create_jinja_environment is the NotImplementedError stub (the concrete subclass supplies the real factory), so any access to jinja_options after first jinja_env access has no effect and accessing jinja_env on App itself fails. create_global_jinja_loader returns DispatchingJinjaLoader(self), which dispatches template lookups between the app loader and each registered blueprint's loader (via iter_blueprints). The debug.setter in this file also touches self.jinja_env.auto_reload, meaning setting app.debug triggers environment creation if it had not happened yet.
units.summary: Lazy Jinja environment creation and the app/blueprint dispatching template loader.

relations.basis: DispatchingJinjaLoader iterates app.iter_blueprints() per graph evidence

uncertainties: Which class actually implements create_jinja_environment, and how jinja_options are merged, is in flask/app.py, not shown

units.explain: Builds the config object for the constructor. Chooses root_path or instance_path depending on the instance_relative flag, copies self.default_config into a dict, overrides DEBUG with get_debug_flag() (environment-derived value), and returns config_class(root_path, defaults). Subclasses overriding config_class or default_config change the outcome; get_debug_flag is an unproven boundary in flask/helpers.py.
units.summary: Construct the Config object rooted at root or instance path with DEBUG default.
uncertainties: Exact environment variable read by get_debug_flag is not in this source

units.explain: Locates the instance folder when the constructor received none. Calls find_package(import_name); if prefix is None it returns package_path/instance, otherwise (installed/ system layouts) prefix/var/<name>-instance using the cached name property. Path joins are os.path-based; no existence check is performed here.
units.summary: Guess the instance folder from the package location or install prefix.
uncertainties: find_package's prefix/package_path semantics live in scaffold.py

units.explain: Returns True when filename is None; otherwise True only when the lowercased filename ends with .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml, or .svg. Comparison is case-insensitive as of 3.2, so uppercase extensions still enable autoescape; any other extension returns False.
units.summary: Enable Jinja autoescape for HTML/XML/SVG templates by extension, case-insensitively.

units.explain: Property pair mapping the debug flag onto config key DEBUG. The getter returns self.config['DEBUG']; the setter writes config['DEBUG']=value and, only when config['TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD'] is None, assigns self.jinja_env.auto_reload=value — which lazily creates the Jinja environment if not yet built. Docstring warns the flag must be set before the server starts for full effect.
units.summary: Debug-mode flag backed by the DEBUG config key, syncing template auto-reload.
uncertainties: Whether config write triggers other DEBUG-dependent behavior (e.g. logging level) is not shown here

units.explain: setupmethod-protected registration of a Blueprint. Records nothing itself; it stores the blueprint in self.blueprints only via the blueprint's own register(self, options) call, passing the keyword options (url_prefix, subdomain, url_defaults, name, etc.) through as a dict for BlueprintSetupState and record callbacks. Guarded by _check_setup_finished via @setupmethod, so calling after the first request raises AssertionError. Duplicate registration with the same name is the blueprint's concern, not visible here.
units.summary: Delegate blueprint registration to Blueprint.register with override options.
uncertainties: How options like 'name' affect self.blueprints keys is decided in Blueprint.register

units.explain: Registers a URL rule. Derives endpoint from the view function when not given (_endpoint_from_view_func) and stuffs it into options. Methods: popped from options; defaults to view_func.methods or ('GET',); a str methods argument raises TypeError; items are uppercased into a set. required_methods start from view_func.required_methods; provide_automatic_options defaults to the view's attribute when present, else 'OPTIONS' not in methods and config['PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS']; when automatic options are provided, OPTIONS is added to required_methods and merged into the method set. Builds url_rule_class(rule, methods=methods, **options), sets provide_automatic_options on the rule object, and adds it to url_map. Finally, if view_func is given, an existing view_functions entry for the endpoint that differs from the new function raises AssertionError ('View function mapping is overwriting an existing endpoint function'); otherwise the view is stored. @setupmethod means the whole operation is refused after the first request.
units.summary: Add a routing rule with derived methods, automatic OPTIONS, and endpoint uniqueness checks.

extras.note: Re-registering the same endpoint with a different view function raises AssertionError, not silent overwrite.
Passing methods as a single string raises TypeError with guidance to pass a list.

uncertainties: Graph could not disambiguate options.pop resolution; reading here assumes dict.pop on the options dict
Whether url_rule_class/map add performs further validation is Werkzeug behavior, not shown

units.explain: Overloaded decorator registering a Jinja filter. Two call forms: @app.template_filter(name) (or bare @app.template_filter — if name is callable, register it immediately via add_template_filter and return it unchanged), or @app.template_filter(name='x') which returns an inner decorator that calls add_template_filter(f, name=name) and returns f. @setupmethod enforces the first-request guard. The inner decorator function and the two t.overload stubs are members of this unit; None name means the function's own __name__ is used (decided by add_template_filter).
units.summary: Decorator (bare or with optional name) to register a Jinja filter.

units.explain: setupmethod that inserts f into self.jinja_env.filters under name or f.__name__. Side effect is direct mutation of the (possibly lazily created) Jinja environment; registering after first access is guarded only by setupmethod's setup guard, and later changes to jinja_options will not rebuild the environment.
units.summary: Register a function as a Jinja filter, defaulting to its __name__.

units.explain: Overloaded decorator registering a Jinja test, structurally identical to template_filter: if the argument is callable, register immediately via add_template_test and return it; otherwise return a decorator calling add_template_test(f, name=name) and returning f. @setupmethod guard applies. Overload stubs and inner decorator are members.
units.summary: Decorator (bare or with optional name) to register a Jinja test.

units.explain: setupmethod storing f in self.jinja_env.tests keyed by name or f.__name__; mutates the live Jinja environment.
units.summary: Register a function as a Jinja test, defaulting to its __name__.

units.explain: Overloaded decorator registering a Jinja global, same dual form as template_filter/template_test: callable argument registers immediately via add_template_global and is returned; otherwise a decorator is returned that registers f under name (or __name__) and returns f. @setupmethod guard applies. Overload stubs and inner decorator are members.
units.summary: Decorator (bare or with optional name) to register a Jinja global.

units.explain: setupmethod storing f in self.jinja_env.globals keyed by name or f.__name__; mutates the live Jinja environment.
units.summary: Register a function as a Jinja global, defaulting to its __name__.

units.explain: setupmethod that appends f to teardown_appcontext_funcs and returns f unchanged (usable as a decorator). Documented contract: functions run when the app context pops (end of request, CLI command, or with-block exit), receive an exception object only when teardown follows an unhandled exception, must not raise (their return values are ignored), and are skipped-for-error only if an errorhandler already handled the exception. Actual invocation lives in flask/ctx.py, not here.
units.summary: Register (and return) a callback run when the app context is torn down.
uncertainties: Invocation order/error passing implemented in flask/ctx.py, outside this batch

units.explain: setupmethod decorator that appends f to shell_context_processors and returns f. The processors' output is consumed by shell setup elsewhere; registration alone has no runtime effect until a shell context is created.
units.summary: Register (and return) a shell context processor function.
uncertainties: When processors are invoked is not visible in this file

units.explain: Error-handler lookup. Computes (exc_class, code) via Scaffold._get_exc_class_and_code(type(e)) where code is the HTTP status code for HTTPException subclasses (None otherwise). Search order: for code handlers first when a code exists (otherwise only the None-class bucket), for each name in (*blueprints, None) — i.e. given blueprints most-specific-first, then app-level — skip empty handler_map entries, then walk exc_class.__mro__ and return the first handler found via handler_map.get(cls). Returns None when nothing matches. Reads self.error_handler_spec; no mutation.
units.summary: Find the most specific registered error handler, blueprint-then-app, code-then-class.
uncertainties: Graph shows two candidates for handler_map.get; reading assumes dict.get on the handler map
The exact ordering/content of the blueprints argument list is decided by callers in flask/app.py

units.explain: Decides whether an HTTP exception should surface as a regular traceback instead of being handled. Returns True if config TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS is set. Otherwise reads TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS: when it is None (unset), debug mode is on, and the exception is a BadRequestKeyError, return True; when truthy, return isinstance(e, BadRequest); otherwise False. Also folded here: the class attribute should_ignore_error = None, a deprecated 3.2 no-op placeholder documented as previously controlling whether errors reach teardown handlers.
units.summary: Determine if an HTTP exception should be trapped (shown as a traceback) per config.
uncertainties: Callers in flask/app.py decide what trapping actually does when this returns True

units.explain: Creates a redirect response by delegating to werkzeug's redirect with location, code (default 303 as of 3.2, changed from 302), and Response=self.response_class so the app's response class is used. No state changes; werkzeug may raise for invalid codes (its behavior, not shown).
units.summary: Build a redirect response using the app's response class, default 303.

relations.basis: response_class is declared on Scaffold per class body

uncertainties: response_class is declared (not initialized) on App; its default value lives in Scaffold

units.explain: Mutable hook for URL building: starting with names=(None,) for app-level defaults, and — when the endpoint contains a dot — appending the reversed blueprint chain of endpoint.rpartition('.')[0] via _split_blueprint_path (parsing the endpoint string because url_for may run outside a request context). For each known name in self.url_default_functions, calls every func(endpoint, values), letting them mutate values in place. No return value.
units.summary: Apply registered URL default functions for endpoint and its blueprint chain.
uncertainties: Ordering guarantees of _split_blueprint_path's output live in flask/helpers.py

units.explain: BuildError fallback invoked by url_for. Iterates url_build_error_handlers calling each handler(error, endpoint, values): a handler returning a non-None value ends the loop and is returned to url_for; a handler raising BuildError replaces the active error with the new one and is skipped; None returns are skipped. If all handlers fail, re-raise: bare `raise` when the (possibly replaced) error is the currently active exception (sys.exc_info()[1]), otherwise `raise error`. This lets custom handlers return substitute URL strings, otherwise the error propagates.
units.summary: Run URL-build error handlers; return a substitute URL or re-raise the BuildError.

extras.note: A handler raising BuildError is skipped and its error becomes the one re-raised if no later handler succeeds.
Only non-None handler return values are used; None means 'not handled'.

uncertainties: Whether the bare `raise` path preserves original traceback chaining depends on CPython semantics, not this source
